# Prototype pollution through keys from HTTP request data (Node.js)

`qualor:js/prototype-pollution` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-1321](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Writes of the form `obj[key1][key2] = value` (one or two levels down, also `++`) where a key that
selects an object comes from the HTTP request (Express, Fastify, Next.js). A single computed write
(`obj[key] = value`), `Object.assign()` and lodash's guarded `merge()`/`set()` are not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
With `__proto__` as the first key, `obj["__proto__"]` is `Object.prototype`, and the second write
adds a property to every object in the process (`constructor` followed by `prototype` reaches it
too). A client can then switch on options such as `isAdmin` everywhere, crash the server, or in
some libraries reach code execution.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the section name from the URL selects an object, and a key is written on it.

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
const settings = {};

app.post('/settings/:section', (req, res) => {
  const section = req.params.section;
  if (!settings[section]) settings[section] = {};
  settings[section][req.body.key] = req.body.value;
  res.json({ ok: true });
});
```

**Compliant:** the data is kept in `Map`s, which have no prototype keys.

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
const settings = new Map();

app.post('/settings/:section', (req, res) => {
  const section = settings.get(req.params.section) ?? new Map();
  section.set(req.body.key, req.body.value);
  settings.set(req.params.section, section);
  res.json({ ok: true });
});
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep data with client-chosen keys in a `Map`.
- Or create the objects without a prototype: `Object.create(null)`, or a literal with
  `__proto__: null`.
- Or allow only known keys: check the key against a constant list (`ALLOWED.includes(key)`) before
  the write.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Express
- Next.js
- Fastify

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A check of the key is recognised only as an allow-list: `includes()` or `has()` on a constant
  array or `Set` of string literals, around the write or as an early return. A deny-list check
  (against `"__proto__"`, `"constructor"`, `"prototype"`) is not recognised, so the write is still
  reported. A key changed inside the checked block is missed.
- Only writes in one expression are seen. An object first taken into a variable and then written
  to, path setters written as loops, and recursive merge helpers are missed.
- Fastify's JSON parser rejects `__proto__` and `constructor` keys by default, but the keys of a
  Fastify JSON body still count as request data.
- Request handlers are recognised by the name of their second parameter (`res`, `reply`, `ctx`,
  `next`, ...): a handler written as `(request, out)` is not checked.
<!-- end: known-limits -->
